title: Neural associations between fingerspelling, print, and signs: An ERP priming study with deaf readers
description: This event-related potential (ERP) study investigates neural mechanisms underlying the integration of fingerspelling, printed English words, and American Sign Language (ASL) signs in deaf readers. Using a priming paradigm with 300 prime-target pairs, the dataset captures electrophysiological responses to identity and translation primes across three modalities, providing insights into cross-modal language processing in the deaf population.
methods_description: Participants were seated in a sound-attenuated room and presented with prime-target pairs while EEG was recorded. Primes consisted of English words (300ms), ASL signs (M=565ms), or fingerspelled words (M=1173ms), followed by four-letter English word targets (500ms). Participants performed an animal detection task using a gamepad. Fixation crosses (800ms purple, 500ms white) preceded each trial.
